content_html:
A toaster is one of the simplest kitchen appliances, but poor slot size, uneven browning or awkward controls can make it surprisingly annoying to use. The right model should fit the bread you actually buy and produce consistent results without taking over the counter.

For this 2026 guide, we looked at models currently highlighted by independent US testing and focused on practical differences between them. We have not carried out our own laboratory testing, so use this as a shortlist to compare and always check the latest product details and owner feedback before buying.

1. Cuisinart Custom Select 2-Slice - versatile everyday choice

Good Housekeeping's 2026 testing highlighted the Cuisinart Custom Select 2-Slice for its consistent results and useful presets for items such as bagels, waffles and English muffins. It also includes a single-slice mode and defrost function.

It is a conventional two-slot model, so buyers who regularly toast very long sourdough slices may prefer a long-slot design instead.

Compare Cuisinart Custom Select listings on eBay

2. Dash Clear View - useful if you want a long slot and visible browning

The Dash Clear View combines a narrow footprint with a long slot and a viewing window, so you can watch the toast as it browns. Good Housekeeping highlighted its value and consistency in testing.

The pop-up action can be forceful, so it is worth reading recent owner feedback if that would bother you.

Compare Dash Clear View listings on eBay

3. Zwilling Enfinigy Long Slot - designed for sourdough and longer slices

The Zwilling Enfinigy long-slot model is aimed at buyers who regularly toast longer artisan bread. Good Housekeeping noted its even results, seven browning levels and presets for bagels, defrosting and reheating.

Its larger footprint and slower cycle time mean it makes most sense if accommodating long slices matters more than saving counter space or shaving seconds off breakfast.

Compare Zwilling Enfinigy toaster listings on eBay

4. Bella 2-Slice Slim - compact option for small kitchens

Good Housekeeping highlighted the Bella 2-Slice Slim for its very narrow design and consistent browning in testing. It is a sensible option for apartments, dorm-style kitchens or anyone trying to keep counter clutter down.

It is slower than some larger competitors and keeps the feature set simple, so it is best for buyers who prioritize space over speed or advanced settings.

Compare Bella 2-Slice Slim listings on eBay

What to look for before buying a toaster

Slot dimensions: Wide slots help with bagels and thick bread, while long slots are better for artisan sourdough and oversized slices.

Counter space: Long-slot designs can be narrow but deep. Check the full dimensions before buying.

Presets: Bagel, defrost, reheat and single-slice modes can be genuinely useful if you use them regularly.

Crumb tray: Easy access makes routine cleaning much less of a chore.

Consistency: Recent independent testing is useful because a toaster that browns evenly across repeated batches is more valuable than one with a long feature list but unpredictable results.

Which one should you compare first?

The Cuisinart is a strong general-purpose starting point. The Dash makes sense if you like the idea of a viewing window and long slot, the Zwilling is aimed at long artisan bread, and the Bella is particularly appealing where counter space is limited.

Prices, offers and availability change regularly. Always check the live listing, warranty, dimensions and returns policy before purchasing.
